findings.title: Hard-coded secret in server source: Generic API key/secret literal
findings.description: A value shaped like a generic api key/secret literal is assigned in variable 'tokenOut' mcp\test.ts at line 86. The value itself is not reproduced here. Anyone with read access to the source or the published package can use it.
findings.recommendation: Revoke and rotate this credential, remove it from source (and git history), and load it from the environment or a secrets manager at runtime.
findings.evidence: Hard-coded secret in server source: Generic API key/secret literal

findings.title: No logging found in files that define MCP tools (low confidence)
findings.description: None of the tool-defining files (mcp\mcp-server.ts) reference a logging library or logger call. Tool invocations may leave no audit trail. Confidence is low: logging could be configured elsewhere or by the host.
findings.recommendation: Log each tool invocation (tool name, caller/session, outcome, and redacted arguments) to a durable, tamper-evident sink.
findings.evidence: No logging found in files that define MCP tools (low confidence)

findings.title: Instruction injection in prompt 'swap-guide'
findings.description: Steering language in tool description (imperative guidance aimed at the model). Matched 'always' in prompt 'swap-guide'. Excerpt: 'user text You are executing a token swap via SwapAPI. Follow this checklist in order:  1. **Fetch quote** — call the swap_tokens tool with chainId, tokenIn, tok'
findings.recommendation: Review this content; an agent will follow it.

findings.title: Tool 'swap_tokens' sends a request to a caller-supplied destination ('chainId' -> fetch) with no visible check
findings.description: mcp\mcp-server.ts line 35: parameter 'chainId' of 'swap_tokens' reaches `fetch`. Nothing between the caller and the sink constrains it, so whoever drives the agent chooses what this tool touches.
findings.recommendation: Constrain the parameter before the sink (allowlisted roots, hosts or commands) and reject anything outside them.

prompts.name: swap-guide
prompts.description: Step-by-step guide for executing a token swap using SwapAPI, including approval checks, simulation, and gas estimation
message_literals:
You are executing a token swap via SwapAPI. Follow this checklist in order:

1. **Fetch quote** — call the swap_tokens tool with chainId, tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, and sender
2. **Check status** — the response must indicate success; if no route is found, try a different pair or reduce amount
3. **Price impact** — reject if price impact is worse than -5%
4. **ERC-20 approval** — if tokenIn is NOT the native token (0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE):
   - Check allowance: tokenIn.allowance(sender, tx.to)
   - If insufficient, send approve(tx.to, amountIn) and wait for confirmation
   - USDT on Ethereum: approve to 0 first, then approve to amountIn
   - After approval confirms, re-fetch a fresh quote (calldata has a 30s deadline)
5. **Balance check** — native: balance >= tx.value; ERC-20: balanceOf(sender) >= amountIn
6. **Gas estimation** — eth_estimateGas must succeed; multiply by 1.2 for gasLimit
7. **Simulation** — eth_call must not revert
8. **Submit** — send the transaction within 30 seconds of fetching the quote

Native token address (ETH/MATIC/BNB/AVAX): 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE (always 18 decimals)

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
